idiom_name: Array of NSLock (or Synchronization.Mutex) stripes; actors for per-key isolation
implementation_notes: Swift ships no striped container, so the manual realization is an array of locks indexed by a stable hash: [NSLock] is the portable Foundation choice, Synchronization.Mutex (iOS 18/macOS 15 or newer) is the modern value-based lock whose withLock { } bracket is compile-time checked, and OSAllocatedUnfairLock is the low-level Apple option. When the per-key resource is isolated state rather than a compound operation, a per-key actor (or one actor owning the keyed dictionary) is the idiomatic replacement, because actors serialize access by construction; striping wins when many keys must not contend and the actor-hop latency per operation matters.
pitfalls: String.hashValue is seeded per process (Swift Hasher), so stripe placement differs between runs; that is fine for in-process striping but must never be persisted, and a fixed-seed Hasher is needed for reproducibility.
NSLock is not reentrant and must be unlocked from the thread that locked it - calling lock twice or unlocking from another thread is a programmer error (NSRecursiveLock exists for recursion).

Actors are reentrant across awaits: an actor method that awaits in the middle can interleave with another call on the same key, so actor-per-key isolation alone does not make multi-step operations atomic.
